_comment: Simulator settings quern writes directly to disk instead of driving the Settings app.
These are undocumented internals: every entry records where it was found and how it was
verified, by runtime. set_simulator_setting applies an entry on any iOS runtime but says so
in its response when that runtime is not under `verified`. scripts/sim-settings-diff.py finds
new ones; see CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/agent-guide.md.
Files are named by alias (see `files`). Each write's `values` maps a state to what is stored;
`read` names the field inside a stored dict that carries the state; `absent` is the state a
missing key means on a fresh simulator. The first write is the one the state is read from;
the rest are the other keys Settings writes for the same toggle, kept in step so nothing
reads a stale copy. Every write happens with the simulator shut down: configuration-profile
restrictions are recomputed at boot, and the keyboard caches its preferences.

password_autofill.title: Password AutoFill
password_autofill.why: When on, iOS offers "Save Password?" after a sign-in: system UI with nothing in the app's accessibility tree, which covers the app and can take the next tap.
password_autofill.settings_ui: Settings > General > AutoFill & Passwords > AutoFill Passwords and Passkeys

verified.method: Written while shut down; Settings showed it off across two reboots, and a first sign-in produced no "Save Password?" sheet.
set_simulator_setting while shut down, then booted: Settings > General > AutoFill & Passwords showed AutoFill Passwords and Passkeys off, where it had been on.
Two simulators switched off through Settings hold the same file, key and value; a direct write was not tried.

does_not_work: defaults write -g AutoFillPasswords: wrong domain, no effect
defaults write com.apple.WebUI AutoFillPasswords NO: persists, but the Settings toggle stays on

auto_correction.title: Auto-Correction
auto_correction.why: The keyboard rewrites words it does not know ("qft list" became "qty list"), so typed text stops matching what a test expects and nothing reports it.
auto_correction.settings_ui: Settings > General > Keyboard > Auto-Correction, and > Hardware Keyboard > Auto-Correction

writes.note: The hardware-keyboard switch. Quern types through the simulated hardware keyboard, so this is the one that governs quern's own typing.

verified.method: Written while shut down; in an app's text field "qft list 1 " became "qty list 1 " with it on and stayed with it off (software keyboard). The hardware-keyboard key was found by quern's diff on 2026-10-07.

set_simulator_setting while shut down, booted, then typed into QuernProbe's field_natural (all text traits at their defaults) through quern, i.e. the hardware-keyboard path: "teh cat " became "the cat " and "qft" became "aft" with it on; both stayed as typed with it off.
Same procedure as on iOS 26.5 (iPhone 16 Pro simulator), same results: on rewrote the trigger, off left it as typed.

auto_capitalization.title: Auto-Capitalization
auto_capitalization.why: iOS capitalizes the start of a sentence, so lowercase text typed into a sentence-style field comes back with a capital ("qft" became "Qft").
auto_capitalization.settings_ui: Settings > General > Keyboard > Auto-Capitalization, and > Hardware Keyboard > Auto-Capitalization

verified.method: set_simulator_setting while shut down, booted, then typed into QuernProbe's field_natural (all text traits at their defaults) through quern, i.e. the hardware-keyboard path: with every other setting off, "hi. there" became "hi. There" with it on and stayed with it off. The first letter of a field was not capitalized either way on this path; the on-screen keyboard capitalizes it.
Same procedure as on iOS 26.5 (iPhone 16 Pro simulator), same results: on rewrote the trigger, off left it as typed.

smart_punctuation.title: Smart Punctuation
smart_punctuation.why: Straight quotes become curly and double hyphens become dashes, so typed punctuation stops matching.

verified.method: set_simulator_setting while shut down, booted, then typed into QuernProbe's field_natural (all text traits at their defaults) through quern, i.e. the hardware-keyboard path: 'say "hi" -- ok' became 'say “hi” — ok' with it on, and stayed as typed with it off.
Same procedure as on iOS 26.5 (iPhone 16 Pro simulator), same results: on rewrote the trigger, off left it as typed.

period_shortcut.title: "." Shortcut
period_shortcut.why: A double space becomes ". ", so text containing two spaces in a row comes back changed.
period_shortcut.settings_ui: Settings > General > Keyboard > "." Shortcut, and > Hardware Keyboard > "." Shortcut

verified.method: set_simulator_setting while shut down, booted, then typed into QuernProbe's field_natural (all text traits at their defaults) through quern, i.e. the hardware-keyboard path: "hi  there" became "hi. There" (with auto-capitalization on) and stayed as typed with it off.
Same procedure as on iOS 26.5 (iPhone 16 Pro simulator), same results: on rewrote the trigger, off left it as typed.

predictive_text.title: Predictive Text
predictive_text.why: Shows the suggestion bar above the software keyboard, which covers part of the screen and can take taps aimed under it.

verified.method: set_simulator_setting while shut down, then booted: Settings > General > Keyboard showed Predictive Text on and off as written. Its effect is on the software keyboard's suggestion bar, which was not inspected.

spell_check.title: Check Spelling
spell_check.why: Underlines words it does not know, which changes how text fields look in screenshots.

verified.method: set_simulator_setting while shut down, then booted: Settings > General > Keyboard showed Check Spelling off as written. The on state was not read back on screen, and its effect (underlining) was not inspected.
